definition: A person with disability who has met the access criteria and is receiving supports through the NDIS.
An individual or organisation that delivers NDIS supports, services or products to participants.
A provider that is registered with the NDIS Commission to deliver NDIS supports and is subject to the Practice Standards for its registration groups.
A category of NDIS supports (e.g. SIL, support coordination) that determines which Practice Standards modules apply to a provider.
The independent Commonwealth agency (the NDIS Commission) responsible for regulating NDIS providers, including registration, audits and complaints.
The set of outcomes and quality indicators a registered provider must meet, covering governance, rights, safety and support delivery.
A specific, checkable expectation that shows whether a provider is meeting a Practice Standard.
An on-site audit by an Approved Quality Auditor for providers delivering higher-risk or more complex supports, assessing practice against the full Practice Standards.
A desktop review (no site visit) used for lower-risk supports, checking documentary evidence of suitability rather than on-site practice.
A follow-up audit partway through a provider's 3-year certification period, checking that practice standards are still being met.
The audit undertaken when a provider's registration is due to expire, to renew registration for a further period.
A follow-up audit or evidence review confirming that all corrective actions from a non-conformity have been completed.
A finding that a provider's practice does not meet a Practice Standard or quality indicator, classified as major or minor depending on severity and risk.
A serious gap that poses a significant risk to participant safety or rights, or reflects a systemic failure to meet a Practice Standard.
A gap against a Practice Standard that is isolated or lower-risk, and does not indicate a systemic failure.
A documented plan setting out how and by when a provider will fix a non-conformity identified during an audit.
A serious incident (e.g. death, serious injury, abuse, neglect, unauthorised restrictive practice) that a registered provider must report to the NDIS Commission within set timeframes.
Any practice that restricts a participant's rights or freedom of movement, which must be authorised, minimised and regularly reviewed.
A plan developed by a behaviour support practitioner that sets out strategies to reduce behaviours of concern, including any restrictive practices used.
The people responsible for the executive decisions or management of a provider organisation, who must meet suitability requirements set by the NDIS Commission.
A role involving more than incidental contact with participants, requiring an NDIS Worker Screening Check or equivalent.
An agreement between a participant and provider that sets out the supports to be delivered, costs, and terms such as cancellation and termination.
A participant's right to make their own decisions about the supports and providers they use.
Support for people who need help with daily tasks to live as independently as possible, usually in a shared living arrangement.
The new SIL registration group under Module 5A, which existing Group 0115 SIL providers transition to as part of mandatory SIL registration.
The Practice Standards module specific to Supported Independent Living, covering governance, safeguarding, workforce, choice and control, and conflict of interest in shared living settings.
Purpose-built or modified accommodation for participants with extreme functional impairment or very high support needs, funded separately from SIL support.
An arrangement where a registered plan manager pays providers on the participant's behalf from their NDIS plan funding.
A provider who helps a participant understand, implement and use the supports and funding in their NDIS plan.
